BLOCKING CONTEXT — OPEN P1 (F21), raised post-budget by the PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 66f1220f. See 120.005-T for the full finding.

This task (T17, the `autoharness run` CLI adapter) depends only on 120.004-T (T15) and is the next link in the runtime chain. Because nothing in the chain depends on 120.005-T (T16, approvals), following this DAG can deliver a complete, shippable CLI path with the local approval/command channel never wired into run_session(). The H2 fail-closed approval guarantee would then be absent from the shipped runtime while every task in the chain reports done.

Do not treat the CLI path as complete until F21 is dispositioned by the operator. Stage changed no dependency edge. Member of 129-S.

BLOCKING — F25 (P1, OPEN, NEW, raised by the twelfth PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD a20c5b50, AFTER the 3-cycle plan-review budget was exhausted).

DEFECT: this is the ONLY task in the entire decomposition that touches the CLI, and it does not define the option contract. Two operator controls are specified elsewhere with NO task obligated to expose them:
- `--force-unlock` is required by 118.005-T (T5, locking.py) and by plan §3.4.
- `--max-restarts N` (restart budget, default 0) and resume-from-cursor are required by 119.006-T (T11, recovery.py).
Neither T5 nor T11 touches `cli.py` — they are `locking.py` and `recovery.py`. This task's tests cover "argument parsing, human and --json rendering, and exit-code propagation for each error kind" but never enumerate WHICH arguments. So every task in the plan can pass its DoD while these controls remain UNREACHABLE FROM THE PRODUCT'S SOLE PUBLIC SURFACE.

THIS IS THE SAME STRUCTURAL DEFECT AS F21 (approvals orderable out of the runtime): a capability is specified in one task, and no task is obligated to wire it to the surface, so the DAG is satisfiable with the capability absent.

WHY IT IS SHARPER THAN F21: `--force-unlock` is the DOCUMENTED REMEDY FOR F22. F22 shows that a post-LOCKING failure — most likely "no copilot exe on PATH" — leaves the workspace locked, and §3.4 says recovery requires an explicit operator `--force-unlock`. If no task is obligated to expose that flag, THE ESCAPE HATCH FOR THE LOCKOUT IS ITSELF UNREACHABLE, and the operator's only recourse is to delete the lockfile by hand. F22 and F25 compound: one creates the lockout, the other removes the exit.

RESOLUTION (operator decision; Stage adopted none): define the COMPLETE `autoharness run` option contract in this task — every flag, its owning module, and its default — and require a test asserting each option is parsed and FORWARDED to `run_session()`. That preserves the no-policy-in-the-adapter rule (the adapter forwards, it does not decide) while closing the reachability gap. Alternative: attach a surface-exposure obligation to each owning task, though that spreads CLI knowledge across shipments and conflicts with this task's ADDITIVE-ONLY / single-adapter framing.

STAGE ADOPTED NO RESOLUTION and changed no dependency edge. Gates 129-S. Detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md (Cycle 4, twelfth Copilot pass).

SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION EVENT — F25 IS RESOLVED AND THIS TASK IS NOT BLOCKED (ruling D, 2026-08-12). This event supersedes the earlier "BLOCKING — F25 (P1, OPEN, NEW)" event on this log, which is preserved above as history and is NO LONGER THE CURRENT STATE. Note that the later estimate_history event did not discharge it; this event does.

WHAT WAS ACCEPTED. The earlier event correctly identified the same structural defect class as F21: capabilities specified in one task with no task obligated to wire them to the product's sole public surface, so the DAG was satisfiable with the capability UNREACHABLE. It was sharper than F21 because --force-unlock is the documented remedy for the F22 lockout, so an unreachable flag would have left the operator with no exit but hand-deleting a lockfile.

CURRENT CONTRACT. THE COMPLETE, STABLE OPTION CONTRACT IS DEFINED HERE, AND THIS IS THE ONLY SURFACE THAT EXPOSES IT: `autoharness run [--json] [--force-unlock] [--max-restarts N] [--pty | --no-pty] [--session-id ID] [-- <verbatim child argv>]`. Each option maps to exactly one run_session() parameter, and tests assert FOR EVERY OPTION both that it parses AND that it is FORWARDED to run_session(). That closes the reachability gap while preserving the no-policy-in-the-adapter rule: the adapter forwards, it does not decide.

ALSO CURRENT (ruling B, 2026-08-12): the remedy this task exposes is enumerated as the gated action `force_unlock` in the FROZEN gated-action catalog owned by 118.003-T, with fallback policy REFUSE — no safe automatic value exists for destroying another holder's lock record, consistent with 118.006-T's refusal on a live holder and on indeterminate liveness. Exact-set-equality tests at 118.003-T and 120.004-T mean this action can no longer be silently omitted from approval routing.

STATUS: NOT BLOCKED. Executable as written; 129-S is not gated by F25.
